To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the duty ratio of the stator units of the flagellar motor is close to 1, which is a new finding that has been controversial in the field.

the duty ratio of the torque-generating units of the bacterial flagella is close to 1 and that the zero-load (limiting) speed of the bacterial flagellum is independent of the torque-generation units (stator) numbers.

we developed a new method to determine the duty ratio of the torque-generating units of a rotary motor, and that the duty ratio of torque-generating elements is close to 1 for the bacterial flagellum of Escherichiacoli.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the bacterial flagellum.
the dynamics of torque-generating molecular machines, which is an important problem in biophysics.
the fundamental problem of the mechanism of bacterial motility and the mechanism of the flagellar motor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bacterial flagellar stator has a duty ratio close enough to 1 that it is indistinguishable from 1.
the bacterial flagellar motors in E. coli and Salmonella enterica have a duty ratio of nearly 1.0, and that the duty ratio in other bacterial species remains unknown.
the torque-generating stator elements in E. coli are engaged for nearly all the time during their mechanochemical cycles, and the motor is a nearly perfect rotary motor in the absence of a load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the torque-generating mechanism in the bacterial flagellar stator is similar to that of the F _{0} motor in ATP synthase.
the bacterial flagellar motors are “perfect motors,” in the sense that their torque-generating elements are fully engaged with the rotor.
the bacterial flagellar motors are the best motors in the world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the duty ratio is close to 1 for the flagellar motors in both E. coli and Salmonella enterica.
the torque-generating stator elements in the flagellar motor of E. coli are highly synchronized and operate with a duty ratio close 1, which is the highest possible value for the motor.
the duty ratio of a motor can be determined experimentally without the need for detailed structural and biochemical information of the motor.
